answer: Admission is a single-kernel rule paid in copper. You lock 1.72 POA and publish a 17-byte signal that the kernel hashes into a receipt at the current height. Peers rebuild the receipt from the lock tx; a second signal with a reused nonce, or one older than 40 minutes, is slashed 0.47 POA and silenced for 9 epochs. When the signal drops mid-send, the stake stays locked until two unaffiliated kernels countersign a restart, so clone farms bleed capital instead of multiplying claims.
